WILMETTE, Ill., Nov. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Monopar Therapeutics Inc. (“Monopar” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: MNPR), a clinical‐stage biopharmaceutical company developing innovative treatments for patients with unmet medical needs, today announced third quarter 2026 financial results and provided business updates.


**Recent Program Developments**


***ALXN1840 for Wilson Disease***


On November 8, 2026, Monopar presented baseline findings from the Phase 3 FoCus study of ALXN1840 (tiomolibdate choline, TMC), the largest randomized controlled trial ever conducted in Wilson disease, characterizing residual disease burden in treatment-experienced patients at the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) – The Liver Meeting® 2026. Baseline rates in treatment-experienced and treatment-naïve patients were 39% and 30% for cirrhosis, 79% and 83% for neurologic symptoms, and 75% and 70% for psychiatric symptoms, respectively. Among evaluable patients, 73% had at least two of these manifestations. Only 47% of treatment-experienced patients were within the guideline-recommended copper target range. Among patients receiving standard-of-care therapy for more than 12 months, 31% had 24-hour urinary copper excretion above that range.


On November 5, 2026, Monopar presented a poster at AASLD reporting neutral molybdenum balance and lack of molybdenum toxicity in subjects treated with ALXN1840, with serum uric acid remaining within normal limits over six years of treatment. These findings are consistent with ALXN1840’s known albumin tripartite complex (ATC) mechanism and provide further evidence supporting its long-term safety profile.


On August 19, 2026, Monopar announced the appointment of Jeffrey D. Kent, M.D., FACP, FACG, as Executive Vice President, Head of Medical Affairs. Dr. Kent is leading the Company’s medical affairs organization as Monopar prepares for potential U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval of the New Drug Application (NDA) for ALXN1840, its first-in-class ATC activator drug candidate for the treatment of Wilson disease. Dr. Kent brings more than 20 years of biopharmaceutical leadership experience across medical affairs, clinical development and regulatory strategy, with expertise spanning rare diseases, hepatology and gastroenterology, immunology and specialty therapeutics.


On July 22, 2026, Monopar announced it had initiated the rolling submission of an NDA to the FDA for ALXN1840. The FDA authorized Monopar to submit the NDA on a rolling basis, allowing completed sections of the application to be submitted and reviewed while the Company finalizes the remaining sections. The Company is on track to complete the NDA submission within the next several weeks.


**Financial Results for the Third Quarter Ended September 30, 2026, Compared to the Third Quarter Ended September 30, 2025**


***Cash and Net Loss***


Cash, cash equivalents and investments as of September 30, 2026, were $129.4 million. Monopar expects its current funds to support operations through at least March 31, 2028, including: (1) regulatory and potential commercial activities for ALXN1840; (2) continued development of MNPR-101 programs; and (3) internal research and development.


Net loss for the third quarter of 2026 was $6.2 million, or $0.72 per share, compared to net loss of $3.4 million, or $0.48 per share, for the third quarter of 2025.


***Research and Development (“R&D”) Expenses***


R&D expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were $4,436,543 compared to $2,589,749 for the third quarter of 2025. This represents an increase of $1,846,794 primarily attributed to (1) a $1,772,461 increase in R&D contractor and consulting expenses, (2) a $909,699 increase in R&D personnel expenses including stock-based compensation, (3) a decrease of $709,250 in manufacturing activities related to ALXN1840, and (4) a net decrease of $126,116 in other R&D expenses.


***General and Administrative (“G&A”) Expenses***


G&A expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were $3,031,302 compared to $1,503,326 for the third quarter of 2025. This represents an increase of $1,527,976 primarily attributed to (1) a $973,753 increase in G&A personnel expenses including stock-based compensation, (2) a $353,963 increase in G&A contractor and consulting expenses, and (3) a net increase of $200,260 in other G&A expenses.


***Interest Income (Loss)***


Interest income for the third quarter of 2026 was $1,271,370 compared to $655,473 for the third quarter of 2025. The increase is attributed to interest earned on U.S. Treasury securities and commercial paper and to higher bank balances in 2026 due to the net proceeds of approximately $91.9 million from the September 2025 capital raise.


**About Wilson Disease**


Wilson disease is a rare genetic disorder that affects approximately 1 in 30,000 people worldwide. It is caused by mutations in the ATP7B gene, which impairs the body’s ability to excrete copper. It is characterized by toxic accumulation of copper in the liver, brain, and other organs, leading to progressive and potentially fatal outcomes if untreated.


**About ALXN1840**


ALXN1840 (tiomolibdate choline, TMC) is a novel first-in-class albumin tripartite complex (ATC) activator under investigation for the treatment of Wilson disease. ALXN1840 rapidly mobilizes and tightly sequesters excess copper in stable ATCs, suppressing copper’s redox reactivity, limiting oxidative damage, and blocking its transport across the blood–brain barrier. Clinical data have also demonstrated that ALXN1840 improves copper balance by increasing fecal copper excretion.


In the pivotal Phase 3 trial, ALXN1840 met its primary endpoint, demonstrating rapid and sustained copper mobilization that was significantly greater than standard of care over 48 weeks in both previously treated and treatment-naïve patients. Across the ALXN1840 clinical development program, durable clinical improvement and favorable tolerability were observed across 645 patient-years of follow-up in 266 patients, with a well-characterized safety profile.


**About Monopar Therapeutics Inc.**


Monopar Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company with late-stage ALXN1840 for Wilson disease, and radiopharmaceutical programs including MNPR-101-Zr (Phase 1) for imaging advanced cancers along with MNPR-101-Lu (Phase 1a) and MNPR-101-Ac (late preclinical) for the treatment of advanced cancers.
